title: "Batch Size"
description: "The number of examples processed together in one training or inference batch."
term: "Batch Size"
letter: "B"
category: "Deep Learning"
difficulty: "Beginner"
---

## Simple explanation

Batch size is how many examples a system processes together in one batch.
For training, it influences how often the model updates its parameters and
how much memory each update uses.

## Technical explanation

If a dataset has $N$ examples and each batch contains $B$ examples, an epoch
usually consists of approximately $\lceil N/B \rceil$ updates when the last
partial batch is retained. The gradient from each batch estimates the
gradient over the full dataset, with variability depending on the data and
sampling.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Batch size affects memory requirements, hardware utilization, throughput,
optimization dynamics, and training duration. For inference, batching
requests can increase throughput but may add queueing delay.

## How it works

The training pipeline groups examples into batches of the selected size.
The model processes each batch, computes a loss and gradient, and the
optimizer updates parameters. A batch that is too large may exceed device
memory; a very small batch may underutilize hardware or produce noisier
gradient estimates.

## Practical example

With 1,000 training examples and a batch size of 100, a complete pass
through the data has 10 batches if the examples divide evenly. Each batch
normally contributes one optimizer update.

## Common misconceptions

- Increasing batch size does not simply make training proportionally faster.
- Batch size and learning rate interact, so changing one may require
  retuning the other.
- The best training batch size may differ from the best inference batch
  size.
